process.title: Your 16-week roadmap to filing
process.subtitle: A structured process where each phase builds on the previous one. You provide the information, MORE builds the file.

phases.title: Induction and Diagnosis
tasks: Induction and diagnosis session to define strategy — MORE
Identify pending documents per evidence matrix — MORE
Draft professional statement — Petitioner
Start management and translation of academic and work documents — Petitioner

phases.title: Professional Statement
tasks: Receive comments from MORE and adjust professional statement
Manage evidence per matrix — Petitioner
Define recommendation letter signatories — Petitioner
Request title equivalency and adjust translations — Petitioner
phases.alert: Second payment due at month completion. Without this payment, the process freezes.

phases.title: Effort Proposal
tasks: MORE develops the effort proposal
Technical review and adjustments by petitioner
Draft recommendation letters — Petitioner
phases.alert: Without the validated proposal from the petitioner, the process cannot continue.

phases.title: Evidence and Executive Presentation
tasks: Deliver final evidence versions (original, translation and PDF) — Petitioner
Sign recommendation letters with signer's CV — Petitioner
MORE develops executive presentation
Send to organizations and chamber of commerce affiliations — Petitioner

phases.title: Implementation Plan
tasks: MORE develops implementation plan
Petitioner reviews and approves
Delivery of signed letters of interest
phases.alert: From the implementation plan, the file must be sent within 4-6 weeks max. Otherwise extra costs for updates will apply.

phases.title: Cover Letter and Exhibits List
tasks: MORE drafts Cover Letter
Complete Intake with petitioner's information
Sign formats and consolidate file — MORE
Final review by petitioner and adjustments

phases.title: Final Submission to USCIS
tasks: Submit complete file to USCIS — MORE

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before taking the step.

items.question: What is the difference between the Turbo Plan and the UPP program?
items.answer: The UPP is a guided self-managed program where you prepare your case with our structured support ($2,500). The Turbo Plan is a done-with-you service where MORE prepares most of the documents with you ($8,000). If you want the highest level of support and the team to build the file for you, the Turbo Plan is the option.

items.question: What if I don't have all the documents ready from the start?
items.answer: No problem. The first weeks of the process are dedicated to identifying which documents you have, which ones need to be obtained, and which require translation. MORE will guide you step by step in getting each one.

items.question: How are the payments structured? Are there installments?
items.answer: The total price is $8,000 USD. Payment is structured in installments during the process: first payment at the start, second payment at month completion (weeks 3-4). If you have questions about payment options, write to us on WhatsApp and an advisor will explain the details.

items.question: What happens if USCIS requests additional documents (RFE)?
items.answer: The Turbo Plan covers the preparation and initial submission of the file. In case of an RFE (Request for Evidence), we can support you with an additional service. However, our thorough preparation aims to minimize the likelihood of this occurring.

items.question: In what language is the file prepared?
items.answer: The entire file is prepared in English, which is the language required by USCIS. Documents in Spanish are officially translated. Translation costs are not included in the plan, but we advise you on how to obtain them.

items.question: Can I start the process if I'm outside the U.S.?
items.answer: Yes, the Turbo Plan is completely remote. Sessions are conducted via video call and all documents are managed digitally. You can start from any country.
